info.name: Notification Service
info.description:
Try the whole product end to end: an administrator onboards a tenant, the tenant sends e-mail, SMS, one-time passwords and bulk messages, follows delivery, and uses its billing and privacy tools.

**Run it:** start the stack (`docker compose --profile app up -d --build`, then `node scripts/seed.mjs`), import this collection and `postman/local.postman_environment.json`, pick the *Notification Service · local* environment, and run the collection from the top (Runner, or `npx newman run postman/notification-service.postman_collection.json -e postman/local.postman_environment.json`). Every request has tests.

Folder 2 creates a new tenant and stores its API key in `apiKey`, so nothing needs copying. To call the client API as an existing tenant instead, set `apiKey` to its key and run folders 3 to 8.

References: client API at `/swagger-ui.html`, `docs/client-guide.md`, `docs/tenant-onboarding.md`, `docs/error-codes.md`.

item.name: 1. Admin · Sign in
item.description: Signs in as a platform administrator and keeps the session token for every admin request that follows.

request.description: Signs in with `adminUsername` / `adminPassword`. The returned token is stored as `adminToken`. Add `verificationCode` when two-factor authentication is on.
The signed-in administrator, their role and any account setup still required.

item.name: 2. Admin · Onboard a tenant
item.description: Creates a tenant from scratch, as in docs/tenant-onboarding.md: client and API key, rate limits, a billing plan, a prepaid account with credit, and its own OTP prices. The new API key is stored as `apiKey`, so the client folders that follow work without copying anything.

request.description: Creates the tenant and returns its API key **once**. Stored as `clientId` and `apiKey`.
Every tenant, with its status, channels and key prefix.
At most 20 client API calls per second for this tenant, with bursts of 40.
At most 10 of this tenant's SMS per second reach the provider. Messages over it wait their turn; nothing is refused.
A EUR plan: SMS 0.008 per message, e-mail 0.001 with 1,000 free per month, 18 % tax. Stored as `planId`.
Puts the tenant on the plan as **prepaid**: each request reserves its cost from credit. Use `POSTPAID` (optionally with `monthlySpendCap`) for monthly invoicing.
Records a 50 EUR payment. The reference makes it idempotent: applying it twice adds nothing.
This tenant pays 0.012 EUR per one-time password on SMS instead of the plan's 0.008. Channels left out pay the plan price; an empty list removes them all.
Every billing account with its plan, mode, balance or cap, and OTP prices.

item.name: 3. Client · Account and error dictionary
item.description: Calls made as the tenant, with its API key in the `X-API-Key` header.

request.description: The tenant behind the API key and the channels it may use. A good first call to check a key.
Every error code with its cause and resolution. Needs no API key.
Look a code up by its error id or its symbolic code (e.g. `INSUFFICIENT_CREDIT`).

item.name: 4. Client · Templates
item.description: The tenant's own templates. Shared templates from the platform are listed read-only.

request.description: A one-time-password template: every send from it is delivered with priority and never after it expires. Stored as `templateId`.
Renders text with sample values and lists any placeholder still missing.
Own templates (`OWNED`) and the platform's (`SHARED`, read-only).

item.name: 5. Client · Send
item.description: Every way to send. Each answer is `202 Accepted`: the request is stored durably and delivered in the background.

request.description: A single e-mail with its text in the request. Placeholders work in `subject` and `body`. Stored as `emailRequestId`.
An OTP from the template created above, valid for 2 minutes. It goes ahead of other traffic and is dropped, not sent late, if it cannot go out in time. Stored as `otpRequestId`.

Up to 50,000 recipients, each with its own values. The `Idempotency-Key` header makes a repeat safe. The last recipient (ending 0400) is rejected by the local test provider, to show a failure. Stored as `bulkRequestId`.

item.name: Repeat bulk with the same key

request.description: The same call again: it returns the original request and sends nothing twice.

exec: pm.test('is a replay of the first request', () => {

request.description: A CSV with a header row: `recipient` is the address, other columns become template values. In Postman, pick `postman/recipients.csv` (or your own file) for `file`.

formdata.value: Hi {{name}}, order {{orderId}} is on its way.

item.name: 6. Client · Track delivery
item.description: Follows what was sent. The first request waits a few seconds for delivery to finish locally.

request.description: The request's status and its message counts per status. `PARTIALLY_FAILED` here: two sent, one rejected.

exec: pm.test('two sent, one failed', () => { const c = pm.response.json().counts; pm.expect(c.sent).to.eql(2); pm.expect(c.failed).to.eql(1); });

request.description: Per-recipient messages, filterable by status and recipient, paged.
The failed recipients as CSV, ready to correct and resend.
The OTP's message, with its category and the moment it expires.

exec: pm.test('is an OTP with an expiry', () => { const m = pm.response.json().items[0]; pm.expect(m.category).to.eql('OTP'); pm.expect(m.expiresAt).to.be.a('string'); });

request.description: Newest first, filterable by channel and your reference.
Message counts per channel and status over the last N hours.

item.name: 7. Client · Senders, billing and privacy
item.description: Sender addresses, the tenant's billing view, and its privacy tools.

request.description: Registers an address to send e-mail from; a confirmation link is e-mailed to it (see Mailpit locally, http://localhost:8025).
Registered addresses and whether each is verified.
The plan, prices (with this tenant's own OTP price), and the credit balance.

exec: pm.test('shows the OTP price', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().rates.find(r => r.channel === 'SMS').otpUnitPrice).to.be.a('string'));

request.description: Every top-up, reservation and refund.
What the month has cost so far (an estimate until it ends).
How long recipient data, message records and idempotency keys are kept.

Everything sent to one person, one row per event with UTC timestamps, for answering a complaint to a data protection authority. Found by any spelling of the address, even after erasure. Never includes message text.
Removes one recipient's address, values and error text from every finished message (e.g. after a data-protection request).

item.name: 8. Client · What errors look like
item.description: Deliberate mistakes, to show the error format: a stable `code`, a numbered `errorId`, `retryable`, and the `traceId` to quote to support.

request.description: Refused with `401 UNAUTHORIZED` (NS-2001).
This tenant may not use WhatsApp: `403 CHANNEL_NOT_ALLOWED` (NS-2008).
One-time passwords are single sends only: `400 CATEGORY_NOT_ALLOWED` (NS-1005).
Refused before anything is sent: `400 INVALID_REQUEST`, naming the value.

item.name: 9. Admin · Operations
item.description: What a platform operator watches day to day.

request.description: Message counts per channel and status, the backlog and request totals.
Every message of one tenant, newest first, with its category, OTP expiry and error id.
Failed messages grouped by kind, channel, client and most common reason.
The SMS, e-mail, WhatsApp and push providers, in failover order per channel.
Every change made through the admin API: who, what, when and the outcome. `ADMIN` only.

item.name: 10. Clean up
item.description: Removes what this run created, so it can be run again and again.

request.description: Requests already accepted keep their text.
Disabling stops every call with its key at once. Clients are never deleted, so their history stays.
Ends the admin session.

variable.description: Set on sign-in so names created by one run are unique.
The tenant API key; set by "Create client", or paste an existing one.
